Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for England Women's reply.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, England Women are on course to seal the series. It would take a miraculous bowling effort from India Women to pull off what looks like an unlikely win at this stage. Join us back in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

It was an absolute nightmare of a batting effort for the Women in Blue. In the first over on the second delivery, Shafali Verma walked back for a duck and it all went downhill for them. Smriti Mandhana handled the situation firmly with a couple of boundaries but it didn't last long as she too had to walk down to her pavilion. The skipper, Harmanpreet Kaur, wasn't able to contribute much to the team and got out in the very next over. Jemimah Rodrigues showed resistance but could not find much support from the rest.

As clinical as it can get! It has been a complete bowling performance from England Women right from ball one and they never let India Women off the hook at any stage. England Women showcased their dominance and discipline with the line and lengths they bowled to ensure no Indian batter could settle and get going. Heather Knight will be mighty pleased with the all-round bowling performance bowling India Women to just 80. Charlie Dean was the pick of the bowlers for her 2 wickets accompanied by Sophie Ecclestone, Lauren Bell and Sarah Glenn who took two wickets as well.

OUT! CLEANED HER UP! Sophie Ecclestone finishes it off! End of India's misery with the bat! Sophie Ecclestone offers flight, full and turning in, at the stumps, Saika Ishaque gets down to hack it across the line but gets beaten all ends up to see her woodwork disturbed. India Women have been bowled out for 80!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the second T20I to commence. The two umpires have made their way out to the middle and they are followed by Heather Knight and Co. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana to open the innings for India Women. It will be Charlie Dean to start with the new ball for England Women. Off we go...

PITCH REPORT - Charles Dagnall is near the deck. He starts by informing that pitch number 7 will be used for the surface. Adds that the square boundaries are 50 metres and 53 metres long while the straight boundary is 63 metres. Anjum Chopra joins him and says that it is a batting paradise and it will be a challenge for the bowlers where they land the ball. Mentions that Indian spinners bowled shorter than their English counterparts. Ends by saying that England's bowlers were more accurate.

India Women's skipper Harmanpreet Kaur says they were looking to bowl as well but mentions that they are okay to bat first. Mentions that they had a positive meeting where they discussed the game plans. Feels that the bowlers are now ready and in good shape. Further adds that they know the area they need to bowl better. Informs that Titas Sadhu was ill and unavailable for selection in the first game but she is now fit and comes in for Kanika Ahuja.

The captain of England Women, Heather Knight says that they will bowl first. Mentions that they got a brilliant start to the series in the first game and there are not many things they did wrong in the previous game. She adds that they would love to sharpen their bowling a bit to make it a perfect team performance. She mentions the only change in their side with Charlie Dean coming in for Mahika Gaur.

England Women (Playing XI) - Sophia Dunkley, Danni Wyatt, Alice Capsey, Natalie Sciver-Brunt, Heather Knight (C), Amy Jones( WK), Freya Kemp, Sophie Ecclestone, Sarah Glenn, Lauren Bell, Charlie Dean (In for Mahika Gaur).

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Shreyanka Patil, Titas Sadhu (In for Kanika Ahuja), Pooja Vastrakar, Renuka Singh, Saika Ishaque.
TOSS - England Women have won the coin toss and they have opted to BOWL first.

On the other hand, Heather Knight's England team will be mighty pleased with their all-round effort that got them over the line in the first match of the series. After a shaky start with the loss of two quick wickets, Natalie Sciver-Brunt and Danni Wyatt stitched up a huge partnership of 138 runs for the third wicket, which proved pivotal in England reaching a mammoth total of 197. Sophie Ecclestone remained the pick of the bowlers for her three crucial wickets. England Women will look to replicate the same performance in this match to ensure they provide another loss to the host nation and seal the series 2-0. Who are you backing to come out on top? Sit tight and stay tuned as we bring you the toss and team news in a bit.

Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. would have looked back at their plans and execution, which failed them in the last match. Nonetheless, the game drew a lot of positives, with most of the batters getting good starts to their innings. The key here in this match will be to convert the starts into bigger scores. Shafali Verma's heroics with the bat, along with Renuka Singh's top spell with the ball in the previous game, will give India the confidence to turn things around in this must-win game. On the other side of the horizon, they would also want to put up better efforts on the field and show character that looked missing in the previous game.

Hello, and a warm welcome to all the cricket enthusiasts out there as we bring to you the 2nd T20I between India Women and England Women to be played at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. This is going to be a do-or-die game for India as they look to bounce back and put up a spirited performance after their 38-run defeat in the first match. Do expect a hard-fought battle that might come down to the wire as Wankhede looks up and is ready to host the big clash of two cricketing giants!
... MATCH DAY ...

The T20I series between the India Women and England Women is going on in full swing as we await the second match which will be played at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. The visitors had come out with the winning result in the first game where the England Women clinched a 38-run win over the hosts. Even after losing Sophia Dunkley and Alice Capsey pretty early on in the match, Danni Wyatt and Natalie Sciver-Brunt kept their cool and took the attack to the opponents. They built a strong partnership which allowed Amy Jones to play freely at the end. While these two showcased their batting prowess, it was Sophie Ecclestone who shone with the ball in her hand. She clinched three important wickets along with some support from Natalie Sciver-Brunt, Sarah Glenn, and Freya Kemp. All in all, it was a pretty dominant performance by the England Women and they will hope to keep their form going for the rest of the tour as well. India Women, on the other hand, failed to capitalize on the home advantage. Renuka Singh did very well with the ball but the other bowlers failed to take timely wickets which allowed the opposition to put up a high total on the board. In the batting unit, it was Shafali Verma who scored a half-century but other than her no one could take the innings deep and failed to build partnerships. The form of Smriti Mandhana and Jemimah Rodrigues will be a topic of concern for the team as well. They will hope to bounce back in this game and regain the momentum. This will be a thrilling encounter. Which team are you supporting?
